findings.text: follow-on: the done-when's central requirement — name the solver commit that moves frame 44 and attribute frames 144, 146, 137 and 179 to a named commit — is unmet. The paragraph names 47f4fe52 and 224a3b96 as candidate mechanisms but states expressly that the ten paired rows prove only the aggregate change and that the data do not isolate one causal commit; the intended frame-44 bracket row at bebd067e produced no receipt and the row at bed0155b was never attempted. The convergence question is answered and the obstruction is recorded, so this is a bounded shortfall the node discloses rather than a silent one, but the plan followup f-mulw-gate-frame-solver-evolution remains open.

follow-on: the falsifiable checks for this 1775-line measurement instrument — 1173-element count, tolerance, non-convergence, finite terminal state, <1e-10 artifact reproduction, device_sha binding, input and geometry equality — live in the run-directory script verify_receipts.py and the asserts in docs/figures/multi-unit-limiter-wall/gate-frame-solver-evolution/render.py, not in the repository test suite. A later edit to measure.py or to the nova.media painters these scripts import would not be exercised automatically. Preserve the corruption and geometry-mismatch cases as focused repository tests; this does not invalidate the recorded refusals for this delivery.

follow-on: render.py's guards are bare assert statements, which are stripped under python -O, so a run with optimisation enabled would draw a panel from unvalidated receipts with no refusal. The measurement and validation scripts are invoked without -O in this node, so the delivered artifacts are unaffected; prefer an explicit raise where the guard is load-bearing for a published figure.
